get.description:
Anyone else sees the rows of the domains they have a role on, without account and server
history (`admin.*`, `maildir.*`, `user.*` except `user.invited`). `domain` follows the console's
domain rules (422 when malformed); one that is unknown or outside the user's domains gives an
empty page. `actor` is a user id, `cli` or `system` (GET /audit-log/actors lists them). `from`
(inclusive) and `to` (exclusive) are ISO 8601 date-times with an offset. `before_id` anchors the
pages: send the first page's newest id with every later page, so rows written in between don't
shift them.
get.summary: What happened on the user's domains, newest first (ties broken by id); a server admin sees every row

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: A domain name in ASCII (punycode) or Unicode, any case: 422 when malformed, an empty page when unknown or not yours.

parameters.name: actor
parameters.description: A user id, `cli` or `system` (GET /audit-log/actors lists them).

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Inclusive: an ISO 8601 date-time with an offset (`Z` or `±hh:mm`); seconds and fractions optional.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Exclusive: an ISO 8601 date-time with an offset, as `from`.

parameters.name: before_id
parameters.description:
The paging anchor: only rows with an id up to this one. Send the first page's newest id
with every later page, so rows written meanwhile don't shift the pages; drop it when the
filters change.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: How many rows a page holds: 10 by default, at most 200. `limit` is accepted too, as on the other lists.

post.description:
The body always carries the `token`. A new person also sends `name`, `password` and `password_confirmation` (the setup rules: 12 or more
characters, not in a known breach when that check is on) and is signed in. An existing user
sends `{}` while signed in as the invited email (409 `sign_in_required` when signed out,
`wrong_account` when signed in as someone else); they are not signed in again. An invitation
that is no longer valid answers 410 `invitation_invalid` with its `state`.

patch.description:
A name alone needs no step-up; an email, role or status does (423 `step_up_required`, checked
after validation: an invalid body answers 422 first). A field that keeps its value changes
nothing. A new email tells the old address and revokes pending invitations to it. Making someone
a server admin removes their grants; changing the role or deactivating signs them out everywhere. 409
`cannot_change_self` when you demote or deactivate yourself; 409 `last_server_admin` when it
would leave no active server admin.

SendWelcomeRequest.description:
The welcome email's recipient and language (POST /domains/{domain}/mailboxes/{mailbox}/welcome).
`to` is one bare address: the endpoint sends mail to an address a manager types, so it must never
carry a display name, a list or a header.

to.description: One plain email address, at most 254 characters: no display name, list or header characters. Sent as typed, trimmed, with the domain lowercased.
